page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the ARM64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The server features 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the r7gd.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core and memory performance. It achieves top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core execution and software compilation with Clang, alongside a top-tier Passmark memory score. Memory bandwidth tests show strong read-only speeds of 6200.09 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 253.52 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Database operations and Redis SET operations also register strong performance, with Redis handling 101.36 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU performance and certain text generation tasks, such as small-model LLM inference, fall into average or poor performance tiers.

The custom ARM64 architecture delivers high resource density and memory bandwidth, offering a qualitatively cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. The combination of 512 GB RAM, dedicated physical cores, and 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage makes this instance highly suitable for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized, ARM64-based instance powered by 64 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this instance delivers top-tier performance in software compilation and memory benchmarks, alongside strong multi-core processing and database operations. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 6200.09 GB/sec for cached small blocks. While single-core performance remains average, the high memory-to-core ratio and fast local storage provide a qualitatively cost-efficient platform for resource-dense deployments. The r7gd.16xlarge is optimized for memory-intensive workloads, including large databases, in-memory caches like Redis, software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving.
